comments.body:
## Pushed for review: Gerrit change 2369

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2369 — `Split the git lock policy out of gitutil`
Change-Id `Idbfc800e0b417fe1649d1edc94e235ab52fc9558`, commit `06b7b0a127673fb8a48777dc9513c1513608cef0`, rebased on `origin/main@4d1567206fb4`. Pushed for review only; NOT submitted. Worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/reb-2359-gitutil-split`, branch `split-gitutil-locking`.

## Gate + prerequisite state

- **file_impact: SET** (it was missing at ticket creation; the coverage gate would have flagged it). 10 paths declared in one `set-file-impact` call — the 2 source modules, the 7 retargeted test files, and `docs/concurrency.md`.
- **plan-review: PASS, signed**, after 4 BLOCK rounds. Each blocker was a real gap in the plan prose, fixed rather than bypassed. No `--force` was used at any point.
  1. AC claimed a RED->GREEN flip on the size test, but at 798/800 it is already GREEN. Reframed, with the measured boundary: 798 PASSES, 801 (three blank lines appended) FAILS, 373 PASSES.
  2. Under-enumerated `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` importers. Re-derived by parsing import nodes rather than grepping: 6 importers, not the 3 originally listed.
  3. Description exceeded the 8000-char admission cap (8080).
  4. Omitted that `git_locking.py` must independently reconstruct `logger`, the `git_outcome` import, and the stdlib imports, since the moved bodies are byte-identical and read them as globals.
- The first signed attestation went **stale** before the claim (`docs/concurrency.md` changed on `origin/main` mid-review). Re-ran the review and claimed back-to-back to close the window. Ticket is `in_progress`, assignee `joeoakhart@navapbc.com`.

## Result

`gitutil.py` 798 -> **373**; new `git_locking.py` **484**. Both inside the 200-500 target; ~427 lines of headroom instead of 2.

## Behaviour-preservation evidence

- `difflib` over the two moved line ranges vs the new module: the ONLY delta is two blank lines at the join. Every moved function body is byte-identical.
- The retained half of `gitutil.py` differs from its pre-split content only in the docstring and import block. No executable line changed.
- On the original base: the same 15 suites ran 194 passed + 1 failed (the failure being the module-size contract test) before, and 195 passed after — the single delta is the cap test. Broader run: 1408 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed.
- On the rebased base: `make lint` exit 0 (complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`), `make typecheck` exit 0 over 688 files, `check_comment_hygiene` / `check_raw_git_writes` / `check_wall_clock_asserts` clean, 254 targeted tests pass.
- Every `rebar` module imports without error, so the re-exports hold for all production importers.

## PER-PATCH EVIDENCE that the monkeypatch retargets are load-bearing

This is the part most likely to be silently wrong, so each site was proven, not asserted. 14 sites across 7 files were retargeted to `git_locking`.

**Structural protection (6 of 7 moved names).** `_retry_probe`, `_reclaim_probe`, `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS`, `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_S`, `_FETCH_COORD_WAIT_S`, `_FETCH_COORD_POLL_S` are deliberately NOT in `gitutil`'s re-export list. Since `monkeypatch.setattr` defaults to `raising=True`, a mis-target is a LOUD failure. Demonstrated by aiming each patch back at `gitutil` and running the owning suite:

| file | mis-targeted name | result |
|---|---|---|
| test_compact_index_lock.py | `_retry_probe` | 2 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_delete_init_index_lock.py | `_retry_probe` | 3 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_event_append_index_lock.py | `_retry_probe` | 1 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py | `_reclaim_probe` | 1 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py | `_reclaim_probe` | 1 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_git_contention_9305.py | `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS` | 1 failed, `AttributeError` |
| test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py | `_FETCH_COORD_WAIT_S` | 1 failed, `NameError` |

**Seeded mutant (the ONE silently mis-targetable site).** `_backoff_sleep` IS re-exported on `gitutil` (its transient-fault retry reads it), so a mis-target there is vacuous rather than loud. For `test_uncontended_write_never_sleeps`, a `_backoff_sleep(0.001)` was seeded into the uncontended path of `_with_index_lock_retry`:
- patched on `git_locking` (correct): **FAILS** — `AssertionError: uncontended happy path must not sleep, slept: [0.001]`
- patched on `gitutil` (the old target), same mutant: **PASSES** — vacuous
That is the exact silent-failure mode, reproduced and closed.

**Invocation probe (patches deliberately LEFT on `gitutil`).** `test_git_outcome.py` patches `"rebar._store.gitutil._backoff_sleep"` in string form; its reader `_with_transient_fault_retry` stayed in `gitutil`, so it must NOT be retargeted. Recording the calls: the `gitutil`-aimed patch **IS invoked**; the same probe aimed at `git_locking` is **never invoked** (fails). `gitutil.run_git` likewise stays — aiming it at `git_locking` gives 5 failures, `AttributeError`.

**Honest non-claim.** Two seams are NOT module-sensitive: `gitutil.os` / `gitutil.subprocess` are the same stdlib module objects as `git_locking.os` / `.subprocess`, so patching either reaches the same object (verified `g.os is gl.os is os` -> True). The `git_locking.os` edit is a readability change, not a behavioural one, and I am not claiming proof for it.

**`getattr` READ channel — a second vacuity path the reviewer caught.** `test_delete_init_index_lock.py:24` and `test_compact_index_lock.py:22` do `getattr(gitutil, "_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S", 300)`. This does NOT raise on a missing name, it falls through — and the real constant IS `300`, so comparing values proves nothing. Proven with a SENTINEL default: `getattr(gitutil, "_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S", sentinel) is not sentinel` -> True, and the value is the same object `git_locking` holds.

## Next session

Wait for `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on 2369, then Submit, then close this ticket. Do NOT close before the change merges.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` is at **798 lines against the locked 800-LOC hard cap** — two lines of headroom. The next change adding three lines fails CI; there is no allowlist and `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked (a contributor change to it fails the build by design).

Not hypothetical: change 2359 (`bd66-28a4-fd31-4c9f`) hit it — 788 on main, +45, CI refused at 833 on all four platforms. It landed by relocating one function and compressing a comment, clearing the cap but leaving 798. Other in-flight changes are growing `src/rebar` modules concurrently.

### What the size test enforces, and where RED begins

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` mirrors the CI gate and enforces **only the 800-line cap** — NOT the 200-500 target. At 798 it is **already GREEN**: this work does not flip it RED to GREEN, it keeps it GREEN with room. Measured: 798 PASSES; 801 (append three blank lines) FAILS with "over the 800-LOC hard cap"; 373 (after the split) PASSES. The RED boundary is exactly **three added lines** away, so the proving evidence is the measured post-split LOC and restored headroom, not a RED-to-GREEN flip.

## The seam — it already exists in the file

`gitutil.py`'s docstring already carves out a policy essay, "Blocking policy under local git lock contention". That is the boundary: **`gitutil` RUNS a git subprocess; the extracted `git_locking.py` DECIDES what happens when git's own locks are contended.** The dependency runs one way (`gitutil` -> `git_locking`).

### What moves

Functions: `_store_git_op_lock`, `_store_git_lock_path`, `fetch_coordination_lock`, `_resolve_common_git_dir`, `_acquire_fetch_coord_flock`, `_with_index_lock_retry`, `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`, `_augment_lock_exhaustion`, `_is_index_lock_error`, `_is_git_lock_error`, `_jitter`, `_backoff_sleep`, `_lock_backoff_s`, `_lock_retry_budget_s`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`.

Module state the moved bodies read as globals, which MUST travel with them: `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S`, `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS`, `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_S`, `_INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_CAP_S`, the `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_*` and `_FETCH_COORD_*` triples, `_LOCK_PATH_RE`, `_LOCK_REF_RE`, and the probes `_retry_probe` / `_reclaim_probe`.

Because the moved bodies stay byte-identical, `git_locking.py` must ALSO independently reconstruct every other module-level name they reference, or they raise `NameError`: its own `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (read by `_store_git_op_lock`, `_with_index_lock_retry`, `fetch_coordination_lock`, `_acquire_fetch_coord_flock`), `from rebar._store import git_outcome` (read by the moved predicates), and the stdlib imports `fcntl`, `logging`, `os`, `random`, `re`, `subprocess`, `time`, `contextlib.contextmanager`, `collections.abc.Callable`/`Iterator`.

### What stays

`run_git`, `run_git_bounded`, `run_git_write`, `_with_transient_fault_retry` + its `_TRANSIENT_*` tables/predicates, `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_AUTOMAINT_OFF`, `_ticket_dirs`, `_dir_is_archived`, `path_is_foreign_to_branch`, `discard_unmerged_paths`.

### Production importers the re-export must keep (found by parsing import nodes)

`_resolve_tracker_git_dir` -> `_commands/` `bridge_repair.py:49`, `fsck.py:57`, `fsck_recover.py:20`, `fsck_repair.py:32`, `fsck_scan.py:43`, `tracker_maintenance.py:99`; `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock` -> `fsck_scan.py:43`; `_with_index_lock_retry` -> `_store/event_commit_git.py:29`; `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S` -> `_store/event_append.py:103`; `_backoff_sleep`/`_jitter` -> `_store/lock.py:71`; `fetch_coordination_lock` -> `_snapshot/git_fetch.py:23`, `_store/sync.py:52`.

### Test consumers, by HOW they depend on a moved name

**(a) `monkeypatch.setattr` on the module object** — retarget to `git_locking`; a mis-target RAISES (`raising=True` default, and the probes/tunables are deliberately not re-exported): `test_git_contention_9305.py`, `test_delete_init_index_lock.py`, `test_compact_index_lock.py`, `test_event_append_index_lock.py`, `test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py`, `test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py`, `test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py`.

**(b) `monkeypatch.setattr` whose READER STAYED** — must NOT be retargeted: `test_git_outcome.py` (string form `"rebar._store.gitutil._backoff_sleep"`) and `test_gitutil_transient_write_retry.py` (`gitutil._backoff_sleep`, `gitutil.run_git`); their readers stay in `gitutil`.

**(c) Direct attribute CALLS/READS** — `gitutil._with_index_lock_retry(...)`, `._reclaim_if_stale_index_lock(...)`, `._is_index_lock_error(...)`, `._store_git_lock_path(...)`, `._jitter(...)`, `._lock_retry_budget_s()` across the same files (one inside a subprocess script STRING). These keep working via re-export and raise `AttributeError` if it is dropped.

**(d) `getattr` READ with a silent default — a vacuity channel that does NOT raise.** `test_delete_init_index_lock.py:24` and `test_compact_index_lock.py:22` do `getattr(gitutil, "_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S", 300)`. Drop the re-export and they fall through to the literal `300` instead of failing — and the real constant IS `300`, so comparing values proves nothing. The proof needs a SENTINEL default. `test_event_append_index_lock.py:40` and `test_txn_index_lock.py:21` read it through `event_append`, which re-exports from `gitutil`, so the same chain must hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes (it passes before the work too; no regression).
- [x] `gitutil.py` is within the 200-500 LOC target.
- [x] `git_locking.py` is within the 200-500 LOC target.
- [x] Every moved function body is byte-identical to its original, shown by `difflib` over the moved line ranges.
- [x] The retained half of `gitutil.py` differs only in its docstring and import block; no executable line changes.
- [x] The same test set passes before and after, with no test going from passing to failing.
- [x] Every `monkeypatch.setattr` whose reader MOVED is retargeted to `git_locking`.
- [x] Every `monkeypatch.setattr` whose reader STAYED is left on `gitutil`.
- [x] Each retarget is shown to be load-bearing by the evidence under Testing.
- [x] Every `getattr(gitutil, <moved name>, <default>)` READ still resolves, proven with a sentinel default rather than by comparing the value.
- [x] Production importers need no change, shown by importing every `rebar` module without error.

## Testing

- Compare moved line ranges against the new module with `difflib`; the diff must be empty apart from join whitespace.
- **`monkeypatch.setattr` is the dangerous part and needs explicit proof.** A patch aimed at the wrong module is **silently vacuous**, not a loud failure. A green suite is NOT evidence. For each retarget, use ONE of:
  - **Mis-target probe** — aim the patch at the module the reader left; the run must fail loudly (`AttributeError`, since the name is absent there).
  - **Seeded mutant** — for a name still present on both modules (`_backoff_sleep`), seed the behaviour the patch observes and show the correct target notices it while the old target passes vacuously.
  - **Invocation probe** — for a patch deliberately LEFT on `gitutil`, record calls and assert it actually fired.
- **`getattr` reads with a default need a DIFFERENT proof**: they fall through rather than raise, and when the default equals the real value the fallback is invisible. Assert with a sentinel default that the name resolves, and is the same object `git_locking` holds.
- Grep for the module path and every moved symbol **as a STRING** (`monkeypatch.setattr`, `getattr`, `importlib`, subprocess script text, docs); an LSP cannot see these, so an empty semantic search is not evidence of absence.
- Run `make lint` (including the complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0`) and `make typecheck` to zero, plus `check_comment_hygiene`, `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`.

file_impact.reason: Loses the git lock-contention layer (its docstring policy essay, _resolve_tracker_git_dir, and lines 203-608) and gains a one-way import that re-exports the moved names; 798 -> 373 LOC. No executable line in the retained half changes.

NEW module: the extracted git lock-contention policy - both advisory flocks (_store_git_op_lock, fetch_coordination_lock), _with_index_lock_retry with its predicates/jitter/backoff, _reclaim_if_stale_index_lock, both test probes, and _resolve_tracker_git_dir. 484 LOC, byte-identical function bodies.
Imports _resolve_common_git_dir/fetch_coordination_lock from the new module and retargets monkeypatch.setattr for _FETCH_COORD_WAIT_S/_FETCH_COORD_POLL_S and the os.open seam to git_locking.
Retargets monkeypatch.setattr for _INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS, _INDEX_LOCK_BACKOFF_S and the lock-retry _backoff_sleep observation to git_locking (their readers moved).
Retargets three monkeypatch.setattr calls on the _retry_probe test seam to git_locking.
Retargets two monkeypatch.setattr calls on the _retry_probe test seam to git_locking.
Two module references updated to the new home: the _jitter/_backoff_sleep seams and fetch_coordination_lock now name git_locking rather than gitutil.
